claims.claim: Delpazolid, which shares the query's 5-(hydroxymethyl)-2-oxazolidinone on a fluorophenyl core, had absolute oral bioavailability of 99.75% after an 800 mg oral dose in healthy subjects, with dose-normalized PO/IV AUC equivalence.

Linezolid, another oxazolidinone with the same fluorophenyl-oxazolidinone attachment, had fasted absolute oral bioavailability of ~100% (103% at 375 mg and 93% at 600 mg), confirming strong fasted absorption in this class.
Milvexian under fasted conditions had absolute F of 54–58% for the SDD formulation and ~100–105% for the oral solution, all well above the 20% threshold.
No transferable record, including the new L2 context records, reports F below 20%; the lowest reported values are ~30% in rats/mice for vorapaxar and zalcitabine, still above the threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental absolute oral bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule.

The query's tetrazole-pyridine-phenyl extension differs from delpazolid's imidazoline and linezolid's morpholine; its effect on permeability and first-pass extraction is inferred rather than directly measured.
Fasted-state data are explicit for linezolid and milvexian, but not explicitly reported for delpazolid; however, delpazolid's near-complete F was measured by IV-referenced absolute bioavailability.
Formulation effects could alter F, but even the lower fasted values in the evidence are well above the 20% threshold.
L2 records are nonvoting context and were not counted as independent gold votes.
